episcopal: relating to a bishop or the bishop's church authority
diocese: district under the spiritual authority of a bishop
bishopric: the office, rank, or district governed by a bishop
archbishop: senior bishop with authority over several dioceses in a region
pastoral: a bishop's formal letter of instruction to his clergy and people
oratory: a small private chapel used for prayer in a house
sacristy: room in a church where sacred vessels and vestments are kept
seminary: school where young men are trained to become priests
curacy: the office or position of a curate, an assistant parish priest
curé: a parish priest in the French Catholic Church
parishes: local church districts each served by its own priest
prebends: incomes paid to church officials from cathedral endowments
perquisites: extra profits or benefits received in addition to regular pay
synod: formal assembly of church clergy to decide religious matters
mitres: tall pointed headdresses worn by bishops in ceremonies
sainted: declared holy, or regarded as saintly and virtuous
venerated: regarded with deep respect, reverence, and admiration
avaricious: greedy for money, wealth, and possessions
benevolence: kindness and a readiness to help or give to others
necessitous: poor, lacking the basic necessities of life
threadbare: worn thin with age and use, shabby in appearance
wadded: padded or stuffed with soft material for warmth
lugubrious: mournful and gloomy, often in an exaggerated way
pontifically: in a pompous, self-important, or priestly manner
dissertation: a long formal written treatise on a particular subject
theological: relating to the study of God and religious belief
gratuitously: without payment, reason, or justification of any kind
mountebank: a dishonest seller of quack medicines who attracts crowds
gendarmes: members of the French armed police force, often mounted
conventionary: member of the French revolutionary National Convention assembly
emperor: ruler of an empire, here Napoleon's imperial rule
prefect: chief administrative official governing a French department
senator: member of the upper legislative chamber of a government
cantons: administrative districts or regions within a country or state
posting: travelling by relays of hired horses along the road
attic: a room directly beneath the roof of a house
alcove: a recess or small section set back from a larger room
sideboard: a long piece of dining-room furniture for holding dishes
chimney-piece: the decorative shelf or frame above a fireplace
bolts: sliding metal bars used to lock doors and windows
bandits: robbers or outlaws who attack travellers and steal from them
lackey: a male servant, especially one wearing a uniform
liveries: uniforms worn by male servants in a wealthy household
pallor: an unnaturally pale, washed-out colour of the face
asthma: a illness making breathing difficult, with wheezing and tightness
gilded: covered with a thin layer of gold or gold-coloured paint
guillotine: machine for beheading criminals, used in France
scaffold: raised wooden platform on which executions were carried out
executioner: official who carries out a sentence of death
wherein: in which, or in what particular respect
therein: in that place, or in that particular matter
hereupon: immediately after this, or as a result of this
hither: to this place, towards the speaker
yonder: over there, at a distance that can be seen
behold: look at or observe something, often in a solemn way
vicinity: the surrounding area or neighbourhood of a place
moor-hens: dark water birds found in marshes and near rivers
vulture: large bird that feeds on dead animals, or a greedy person
orphans: children whose parents have died and who are cared for by others
beggars: people who live by asking others for money or food
tolerable: bearable or acceptable, though not especially good
dined: ate the main meal of the day, usually in the evening
suite: a set of connected rooms, or a group of attendants
thunderbolt: a sudden shock, or a flash of lightning with thunder
mounted: riding on horseback, or set up on a support
wretch: a deeply unhappy or miserable person, or a contemptible one
